CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

This is Jeremy R. Winget’s personal website (jrwinget.com), built with Quarto and deployed via Netlify. The site is a multi-section personal website featuring a blog, research publications, software projects, talks, and courses.

Key Commands

Building and Previewing

# Preview the site locally (starts development server)
quarto preview

# Render the entire site
quarto render

# Render a specific file
quarto render path/to/file.qmd

# Render only changed files (uses freeze cache)
quarto render --cache refresh

Deployment

Deployment is automated through Netlify using the @quarto/netlify-plugin-quarto plugin. The site automatically builds and deploys on push to the main branch. The build output directory is _site/.

Content Structure

Blog Posts

  • Location: blog/YYYY-MM-DD_slug/index.qmd
  • Each post is a directory containing index.qmd and associated assets (images, data, etc.)
  • Blog listing page: blog.qmd (auto-generates from all blog/*/index.qmd files)
  • Posts use YAML frontmatter with fields: title, subtitle, date, categories, tags, image, toc, citation, and aliases
  • The freeze: auto setting in _quarto.yml means posts with code are only re-executed when the source changes

Other Content Sections

  • Research: research/ - Research projects and publications
  • Software: software/ - Software packages and tools (e.g., {bidux}, {consensys}, {proximal})
  • Talks: talks/YYYY_slug/ - Conference talks and presentations
  • Courses: courses/ - Teaching materials (e.g., PSYC courses)

Each section has: 1. A listing page at the root (e.g., research.qmd) 2. Individual subdirectories with index.qmd files

Technical Architecture

Quarto Configuration (_quarto.yml)

The site uses Quarto’s website project type with: - Engine: knitr (for R code execution) - Execution: freeze: auto - Only re-renders when source changes - Theme: Custom theme based on Flatly with custom SCSS (assets/main.scss) and CSS (assets/styles.css) - Comments: Utterances integration (GitHub Issues-based comments) - Analytics: Plausible.io integration for privacy-friendly analytics - Features: Search, RSS feed, OpenGraph/Twitter cards, cookie consent

URL Redirects

The make-redirects.R script generates Netlify-style redirects: - Creates short URLs by stripping date prefixes from blog posts and talks - Example: /when-groups-get-stuck → /blog/2025-10-31_when-groups-get-stuck - Run this script after adding new posts/talks to update _site/_redirects - The script uses the {here} package for path management

Styling and Assets

  • SCSS: assets/main.scss - Main theme customizations
  • CSS: assets/styles.css - Additional styles
  • Images: assets/img/ - Site-wide images (logo, icons)
  • 404: Custom 404 page defined in assets/404.md

Navigation Structure

The navbar (defined in _quarto.yml) has: - Left: Blog, Research, Projects dropdown (Software, Talks, Courses) - Right: Social links (GitHub, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Email) - Footer: Copyright, license info, contact, RSS link

Development Workflow

Adding a New Blog Post

  1. Create a new directory: blog/YYYY-MM-DD_short-slug/
  2. Add index.qmd with proper YAML frontmatter
  3. Include any images or data files in the same directory
  4. Run quarto render to build
  5. Optionally run Rscript make-redirects.R to update short URL redirects

Working with Code Chunks

  • R code chunks are executed via knitr
  • Results are cached in .quarto/_freeze/ when freeze: auto is enabled
  • To force re-execution, delete the relevant freeze cache or use quarto render --cache refresh
  • Code chunks default to echo: true and output: true (both code and results shown)

Content Features

Margin Notes & Asides

Margin notes are a powerful way to add supplementary information, definitions, or commentary without disrupting the main narrative flow. They appear in the right margin on large screens and gracefully collapse to inline elements on mobile devices.

Syntax Options

Option 1: Column Margin (Recommended)

::: {.column-margin}
This supplementary information appears in the margin.
You can use **formatting** and [links](https://example.com).
:::

Option 2: Aside

::: {.aside}
Alternative syntax that also creates a margin note.
:::

When to Use Margin Notes

  • Definitions: Clarify technical terms or jargon without interrupting flow
  • Citations: Add brief context about referenced researchers or studies
  • Examples: Provide concrete illustrations of abstract concepts
  • Cross-references: Point to related content or resources
  • Commentary: Offer meta-commentary or editorial asides

Styling

Margin notes automatically: - Display at 85-90% of body text size - Use a muted color palette (#5a5a5a) for reduced visual weight - Include a warm brown left border (#d4a574) matching the site aesthetic - Have semi-transparent white backgrounds for subtle differentiation - Collapse to inline, bordered boxes on screens < 992px wide - Support full markdown formatting including bold, italics, and links

Best Practices

  • Keep margin notes concise (1-3 sentences ideal)
  • Use them sparingly to maintain their impact
  • Place them adjacent to the related main text
  • Ensure they’re truly supplementary (not essential to understanding)
  • Test readability on both desktop and mobile views

Examples from the Site

See the “When Groups Get Stuck” blog post for working examples: - Definition of the hidden-profile problem (using .column-margin) - Context about Moscovici’s research findings (using .aside)

Local Development

# Start preview server (auto-refreshes on changes)
quarto preview

# The site will be available at http://localhost:XXXX
# Changes to .qmd files trigger automatic re-rendering

Important Files

  • _quarto.yml - Main configuration file for the entire site
  • netlify.toml - Netlify deployment configuration
  • _publish.yml - Publishing configuration (Netlify site ID)
  • make-redirects.R - Generates URL redirects for short URLs
  • _redirects - Static redirects file (also generated dynamically)
  • .gitignore - Excludes _site/, _freeze/, .quarto/, node_modules/

Extensions

The site uses Quarto extensions located in _extensions/quarto-ext/. These provide additional functionality for rendering and formatting.

Notes

  • The site is primarily content-focused with minimal custom JavaScript
  • R is required for rendering posts with R code chunks
  • The {here} package is used in R scripts for robust path handling
  • Comments on blog posts are stored as GitHub Issues in the repository
  • RSS feed is automatically generated at /blog.xml
